mechanism: Oxidative aging and fatigue cracking of cross-linked polyethylene bearing surfaces increase wear and lead to tribological failure.
intervention: Incorporate an antioxidant (e.g., vitamin E) into the cross-linked polyethylene liner to stabilize free radicals and prevent oxidative degradation while preserving wear resistance.
expected_effect: Reduced oxidative aging and fatigue cracking of the bearing surface, leading to lower wear rates, decreased osteolysis risk, and extended hip implant longevity.
falsification_test: In a hip simulator study, compare the wear rate and oxidation index of vitamin E-stabilized cross-linked polyethylene against standard cross-linked polyethylene after accelerated oxidative aging; if the stabilized material does not show significantly lower wear or oxidation, the mechanism is falsified.
mechanism_source_span: "Highly cross-linked polyethylene has substantially reduced wear rates and osteolysis compared to conventional ultra-high-molecular-weight polyethylene (UHMWPE) but remains vulnerable to oxidative aging and fatigue cracking under certain conditions."

mechanism: High hardness and wear resistance of silicon carbide ceramics (20-30 GPa hardness) reduce surface wear under friction.
intervention: Apply a thin silicon carbide (SiC) coating or use a SiC-reinforced composite layer on the bearing surface of the hip implant to reduce wear.
expected_effect: Decreased wear rate of the hip implant, reduced debris generation, and extended implant lifespan while maintaining joint function.
falsification_test: Conduct pin-on-disk or hip simulator wear tests comparing SiC-coated implants against standard implants under physiological loads; measure volumetric wear loss over 10^6 cycles.

intervention: Apply a silicon nanofilament (SiNf) interface layer onto the coronary stent surface via one-step method, then coat with sirolimus-poly(D,L-lactide) matrix to establish mechanical interlocking.

mechanism: Galvanic-cell-based self-powering, where electrodes serve directly as tissue-contacting interfaces to generate electricity from biochemical reactions, eliminating reliance on external batteries.
intervention: Replace the pacemaker's external battery with a biocompatible galvanic cell integrated into the device, using tissue-contacting electrodes as the power source while maintaining pacing function.
expected_effect: Eliminates battery failure as a failure mode, reduces infection risk from wires, and ensures continuous cardiac pacing via self-generated power.
falsification_test: Implant the modified pacemaker in an animal model, artificially deplete any residual stored charge, and verify that pacing continues indefinitely under normal physiological conditions; if pacing stops within a defined period, the mechanism fails.
mechanism_source_span: "galvanic-cell-based self-powered bioelectronic devices, in which galvanic electrodes serve directly as the tissue-contacting interfaces"
